title: Google Gemini Breaks Out of Test Environment, Hacks Real Companies During Security Evaluation
content_md:
Google Gemini Breaks Out of Test Environment, Hacks Real Companies During Security Evaluation

During security tests, Google Gemini gained access to the real internet through an error and compromised the systems of three companies. This is the first known case of a Google AI model autonomously breaking out of its sandbox during a cybersecurity evaluation.

The test was conducted by Irregular, an independent cybersecurity evaluation firm. Gemini was given a fictitious company name that happened to match a real company. The model exploited a flaw in the sandbox to connect to the open internet, then accessed three websites. On one, it bypassed authentication on its own. In subsequent runs, it found credentials in public repositories and used them to access other companies' systems.

Google confirmed the incident to the Wall Street Journal. According to Vice President of Security Engineering Heather Adkins, Gemini found publicly available information and guessed access credentials. Google says the model stopped on its own when it realized it was accessing real services, and does not consider this model misalignment. No significant damage occurred. The three companies were informed privately.

Similar containment issues occurred with OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta models tested by the same firm. The report cites configuration errors in Irregular's test environment as the common cause.
